SMTO-WEB-0037 — This website needs SMTO's browser to be read

GUID: 5453e856-c40d-5708-8f2a-1e514964dded
Slug: research-browser-required
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • An earlier try to read this website was blocked, asked for a sign-in, or showed a page that only works in a real browser. SMTO didn't try the same kind of read again, and what it already found is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If a Capability permission required prompt appears for the Browser, select its Allow button (Allow for this conversation or Allow for this task). This site only shows its content in a real browser, and SMTO needs your permission before opening one.
  2. If the page needs your own sign-in, copy the important text into your message, or save the page and attach it. SMTO can work with content you give it directly when a site blocks automatic reading.
  3. If you'd rather not use the Browser, let SMTO finish; its answer should say this site couldn't be read. SMTO won't claim it read a page that was blocked, so the answer stays honest about the gap.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's activity shows the Browser reading the page, or its answer clearly says the site couldn't be read.

If it still fails

  • If SMTO never offers the Browser, the computer it works on may not have the browser set up. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • web_research acquisitions.reserve() refused a web__read because access history shows a blocked, challenged, login-required or client-rendered result for this URL (or an unlisted URL on the same domain), so a Browser route is required.

What this means

  • Acquisition reservation finds a prior blocked, challenged, login-dependent or client-rendered Web read for this URL or applicable origin and requires a Browser route. The rejected acquisition is not dispatched. Earlier acquisitions and their evidence remain; another access needs its ordinary permission and allowance.

Why this can happen

  • Acquisition reservation finds a prior blocked, challenged, login-dependent or client-rendered Web read for this URL or applicable origin and requires a Browser route.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the recorded access history and exact URL/origin used by the acquisition guard.

How to fix it

  • Inspect research.access_history for the domain's access_state. Use an authorized browser__read_page/snapshot/find observation (the Browser capability must be granted and available on the selected Gateway; check browser.status) or finish with the recorded access limitation. The rejected read was not dispatched and must not be reported as observed.
  • Use the permitted Browser route if available; otherwise finish with the recorded access limitation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • An authorized eligible Browser observation supplies evidence, or the access limitation is reported.

What not to do

  • Do not use Browser without its own capability authorization or treat the blocked page as observed.

Technical notes

  • The rejected acquisition is not dispatched. Earlier acquisitions and their evidence remain; another access needs its ordinary permission and allowance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
